action: Place probe to obtain a view of the bladder.

interpretation: Correct the image quality because the screen appears 'bright white' due to excessive gain.

action: Maintain probe position and assess the image after gain adjustment.
interpretation: Confirm clear visualization of the bladder in preparation for measurement.

action: Select the 'pre-void volume' function on the machine interface. Tap the center of the bladder on the screen.
Verify the placement of the auto-adjusted calipers to measure dimensions.
interpretation: Measuring the width and height of the bladder in the current view.
Store the transverse measurements for the volume calculation.

action: Unfreeze the image. Rotate the probe to obtain a sagittal view.
interpretation: Transition from transverse to the sagittal plane.

action: Orient the probe marker towards the patient's head. Tilt and rock the probe towards the patient's feet.
interpretation: Adjust the probe angle to visualize the 'whole bladder'.

action: Fan through the bladder to locate the widest cross-section. Freeze the image. Measure the length.
interpretation: Identify the 'biggest orientation' with the 'biggest volume' to ensure accurate length measurement.
